standard_text: Pre-number concepts: describing position (top, bottom, inside, outside, near, far, left, right), comparing groups (more, fewer, same) and sorting objects (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 1)
meta_desc: Class 1 Finding the Furry Cat worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 1): position words, left and right, more and fewer, and sorting. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Where is it? On, under, inside, next to.
key_sub: Compare groups: more, fewer or the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Position words tell where things are: on, under, inside, next to, behind.
  • Your left hand and right hand help you tell left from right.
  • Match things one to one to see which group has more.

Examples

Example

The cat is under the table. Where is the table?

The table is above the cat

Answer: Over the cat

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up left and rightHold up your right hand: right is that side.
Saying the group of bigger things has moreCount or match them: more means a bigger number.

faq.a: Ideas children need before counting well: position, size, more and fewer, and sorting.

faq.q: How can I practise left and right?
faq.a: Play games like 'Touch your left ear' and talk about where things are in the room.

items.q: Where is the ball?

items.e: The balloon is above the table. It is higher than the table, but it does not touch it. It is not on the table.

items.q: Where is the ball?
items.e: We can see all of the ball. It hides part of the box. It is nearer to us. It is in front of the box.

items.q: Which box has the most apples?
items.e: Count each box: A has 10, B has 5, C has 3, D has 4. 10 is the biggest number, so box A.
Count each box: A has 3, B has 7, C has 9, D has 8. 3 is the smallest number, so box A.

items.q: Which box has the most balls?
items.e: Count each box: A has 8, B has 6, C has 5, D has 9. 9 is the biggest number, so box D.
Count each box: A has 6, B has 7, C has 5, D has 10. 5 is the smallest number, so box C.

items.q: Which box has the most fish?
items.e: Count each box: A has 10, B has 7, C has 4, D has 6. 10 is the biggest number, so box A.

items.q: Which box has the fewest flowers?

Count each box: A has 10, B has 5, C has 9, D has 8. 10 is the biggest number, so box A.

items.q: Which box has the fewest ducks?

items.q: Which box has the most cups?

items.q: Which box has the most apples?

items.q: Are there more apples or more cups?
items.e: Match them one to one. Some apples have no partner, so there are more apples. More apples.
